text:
26:27 I got confused at this point.

@kunal Kushwaha

Correct me if am wrong.

Memory from heap is only allocated when we use the "new" keyword.

For example if i say

class Person{
}

now when I'll create Person Class instance

Person person = new Person();

so at this time person instance stores the address of newly created object and it will be stored in the heap memory. person instance lies in the stack and it will point on the newly created object which lies in the heap.

but when i say it with primitive data types like

int num = 10;

at this time num is stored inside the stack and and its value is 10. At this time num is not a reference variable and does not pointing anywhere. It is a variable of primitive data type. In Java, primitive data types (like int, float, char, etc.) directly store their values in the memory location of the variable itself, and they are stored in the stack memory.

text:
For my own future reference:
Static language - data type is defined and it is checked at compilation. eg - java
Dynamic language - data type is not defined and it is checked at the runtime. eg - python
The variable is stored in stack memory, the object or the value of that variable is stored in the heap memory
An object can have multiple reference variables and when a change is made to the object by any reference variable, it is visible to all the reference variables pointing towards that object

Memory from heap is only allocated when we use the "new" keyword.

For example if i say

class Person{
}

now when I'll create Person Class instance

Person person = new Person();

so at this time person instance stores the address of newly created object and it will be stored in the heap memory. person instance lies in the stack and it will point on the newly created object which lies in the heap.

but when i say it with primitive data types like

int num = 10;

at this time num is stored inside the stack and and its value is 10. At this time num is not a reference variable and does not pointing anywhere. It is a variable of primitive data type. author: @sagarbhadouria5915
text:
very good video with great and easy to understand explanation. Just want to mention one thing which is not correct in this video for Java.
1. memory management strategies can change with change in programming languages e.g. in Java local/primitives variables always get stored in stack memory.
so what kunal is explaining in this video(25:30) applies to Python but not to Java i.e. int a=10; whole thing will be stored in stack memory in Java.

also below point are for better understanding of Heap and Stack memory as in video I found it little bit confusing:
1. Stack and Heap memory are actually regions of memory in RAM created by OS during execution of a program.
2. Stack memory is a contiguous block of memory, used for storing temporary variables created by a program during its execution.
3. Heap memory is a pool of memory, used for dynamic memory allocation during the program's execution.
4. When a program executes, the operating system allocates a block of memory for the program to use and then OS divides this memory block into multiple regions like Code segment or text segment, Data segment, BSS segment, Stack and Heap for the execution purpose of program. So this is how actually Stack and Heap memory gets created in RAM by OS.
5. The size of the stack and heap memory regions is determined by the program's requirements and the amount of available memory(RAM) on the system.
6. size of Stack memory is generally much smaller than the Heap, and access to Stack memory is faster.
